name: Parah Adumah Ritual Procedure
notes: Detailed procedure for burning the red heifer: slaughter, blood sprinkling, burning with cedar/hyssop/scarlet, collection and division of ashes — distinct from the general parah adumah entry

name: Preparation of Mei Chatat (Mixing Ashes with Water)
notes: Rules governing the mixing of red heifer ashes with water: valid/invalid vessels, intention, work during preparation, multiple simultaneous preparations

name: Sprinkling of Mei Chatat (Haza'ah)
notes: Laws of sprinkling the purification waters: use of hyssop, valid/invalid sprinklers, intention during sprinkling, sprinkled on multiple objects, dripping water

name: Madaf Uncleanness (for Mei Chatat)
notes: Special stringency for purity of mei chatat whereby objects that are susceptible to midras are treated as if they have madaf-level uncleanness; unique to the hatat domain

name: Hyssop (Ezov) for Purification
notes: Rules for valid hyssop used in mei chatat sprinkling: species requirements, invalid named varieties, minimum quantity, stalks and buds, combination with thread and spindle-reed

name: Factors Invalidating the Red Cow
notes: Conditions that disqualify the red heifer: non-red hairs, riding/leaning on it, use for labor, being mounted by a male, pregnancy, purchase from non-Jews, etc.

name: Priest's Purity Status for Red Heifer Ceremony
notes: Seven-day separation, sprinkling on the officiating priest, deliberate defilement to counter Sadducee view, immersion and sunset requirements for the burning priest

name: Red Heifer Ceremony on Mount of Olives
notes: The ramp from Temple Mount to Mount of Olives, the place of burning, procedures at the Mount of Olives including the immersion pool and the burning site

name: Children Raised in Purity for Mei Chatat (Shiloah)
notes: Special institution of raising children in purity over rock-hewn courtyards to draw water from the Shiloah spring for sanctifying the mei chatat ashes

name: Division and Storage of Red Heifer Ashes
notes: Division of ashes into three parts: one on the chel, one on the Mount of Olives, one distributed among priestly watches; historical list of who prepared each of the nine cows

name: Work Invalidating Mei Chatat
notes: Any work performed while drawing, carrying, or mixing the hatat waters invalidates them; detailed rules about what constitutes work and exceptions

name: Stringency of Mei Chatat Purity (Middat Chumra Hapacha leKula)
notes: The paradox that those engaged with the red heifer become impure themselves even though the rite purifies others; stringencies of hatat purity that end up being lenient

name: Fitness of Water for Mei Chatat
notes: Which water sources are valid for mei chatat: living vs. drawn water, mixed waters (Jordan/Yarmuk), marsh waters, spoiled/salty water, well water with sediment

name: Vessels for Hatat Waters
notes: Rules for valid vessels to collect and hold mei chatat: earthenware, stone, dung vessels, boat; what counts as a vessel vs. not (cupped hands, wall of vessel, stopper)

name: Stone Trough for Hatat Waters
notes: Laws specific to stone troughs fixed to the ground vs. moveable, dual troughs, holes in troughs, clay rims — their status for drawing, mixing and sprinkling hatat waters

name: Age Requirements for Sacrificial Animals
notes: Minimum and maximum age for various sacrifices: lambs, rams, bulls, calves; day-counting from birth; the palges/noked status of animals 13 months old

name: Palges (Animal in Transitional Age Status)
notes: Animal between one and two years old (13 months), called palges (R. Tarfon), noked (Ben Azzai), parakhrigma (R. Ishmael); neither valid as lamb nor ram; brings ram libations but not counted as offering

name: Requirement that Omer and Two Loaves Come from Eretz Yisrael
notes: Exception to the rule that congregation offerings may come from outside the land or from old produce: the omer and the two loaves of Shavuot must come from new produce within Eretz Yisrael

name: Defilement of Garments by Red Heifer Participants
notes: All who participate in the red heifer rite defile their garments; the paradox that the cow itself does not defile garments but those who handle it do

name: Levels of Ritual Impurity Transmission (Rishon, Sheni, Shlishi)
notes: The graded transmission of impurity from primary (av hatumah) through first, second, third degree; how liquids that become unclean defile vessels at higher degrees than their own source

name: Tightly-Fitting Cover (Tzamid Patil) for Hatat Waters
notes: Whether a tightly-fitting cover protects hatat waters from impurity; distinction between sealed water that has been prepared vs. unprepared water

name: Intention Affecting Validity of Hatat Waters
notes: Changed intention during drawing or mixing (switching from one mixture to multiple or vice versa), intending to drink hatat water, intending to store vs. pour water — effect on validity
